artists.biography: Salad were a UK-based alternative rock group formed in London in 1992, that included Dutch vocalist/keyboardist Marijne van der Vlugt, bassist Pete Brown, drummer Rob Wakeman (ex-Colenso Parade), and guitarist Paul Kennedy. In 1996, Charley Stone (later of Gay Dad) joined the band as a live guitarist, keyboard player and backing vocalist.
artists.name: Salad

Salad.biography: Salad were a UK-based alternative rock group formed in London in 1992, that included Dutch vocalist/keyboardist Marijne van der Vlugt, bassist Pete Brown, drummer Rob Wakeman (ex-Colenso Parade), and guitarist Paul Kennedy. In 1996, Charley Stone (later of Gay Dad) joined the band as a live guitarist, keyboard player and backing vocalist.

perplexity.description:
Ice Cream is the third studio album by British alternative rock band Salad, originally released in 1997. The album showcases the band’s signature blend of jangly guitar-driven melodies, dynamic rhythms, and infectious pop hooks, firmly rooted in the Britpop and indie rock movements of the mid-1990s. Salad’s sound on Ice Cream is characterized by its energetic arrangements, playful lyrics, and the distinctive vocals of Marijne van der Vlugt, creating a vibrant and accessible record that stands out in the era’s crowded rock landscape.

As the follow-up to their successful debut Drink Me (1995), Ice Cream further established Salad’s reputation for crafting catchy, guitar-based pop with a quirky edge. While not as commercially dominant as some of their contemporaries, the album solidified the band’s cult following and remains a fan favorite for its spirited songwriting and memorable tracks. Upon its original release, Ice Cream received positive reviews for its inventiveness and charm, with critics noting its ability to balance mainstream appeal with a distinct personality. The album’s enduring appeal is reflected in its continued recognition among fans of 1990s British rock.
